name: Saint Andrew the Apostle
history: A fisherman of Bethsaida, disciple of John the Baptist, and the first apostle called by Christ. He brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus. Tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras in Greece, the saltire of Scotland's flag.
fast: The traditional Saint Andrew Christmas Novena begins today: 'Hail and blessed be the hour and moment in which the Son of God was born…', said fifteen times a day until Christmas.
meditation: Andrew's first act as a disciple was to bring someone else to Jesus. Whom will you bring?
life: Andrew was a fisherman from Bethsaida who worked with his brother Simon on the Sea of Galilee. Saint John's Gospel tells that he was a disciple of John the Baptist, and that when the Baptist pointed to Jesus as the Lamb of God, Andrew followed Him and asked where He was staying. 'Come and see,' Jesus answered, and Andrew spent the day with Him. He went at once to tell Simon, 'We have found the Messiah.' Later it was Andrew who found the boy with five barley loaves and two fish, and who, with Philip, brought some Greeks to Jesus. Tradition holds that he preached around the Black Sea and in Greece and was crucified at Patras. He is the patron of Scotland, of Greece and of the Church of Constantinople, and his feast is a day of friendship between Rome and the Orthodox.
prayerTo: Saint Andrew, you left your nets when Christ called and went at once to bring your brother to Him. Pray for me, that I may follow the Lord without delay and share Him with those I love. Pray for the unity of Christians of East and West, and for the people of Scotland. Amen.
penance: Invite someone to Mass, or speak a word about your faith to one person who does not know Christ. Pray for the unity of Christians.
prayer: We humbly pray Your majesty, O Lord, that, as blessed Andrew was a preacher and ruler in Your Church, so he may always intercede for us with You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
